about: Prerequisite map for P1 Energy (brief docs/briefs/2026-11-15-script-four-topics.md, B1, 2026-11-17): every idea the seven scripted lessons use, what each depends on (maths included), and where it is taught. Lessons run in syllabus order: p1-energy-stores, p1-kinetic-potential, p1-conservation, p1-efficiency, p1-power, p1-heating, p1-national-grid. P1 comes before P2 in the syllabus, so a P1 script recalls a P2 idea only if the lesson itself re-teaches it. Used when scripting: each script teaches or recalls an idea before it asks about it.

ideas.name: Energy, measured in joules (J)
The energy stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, thermal, chemical, magnetic, electrostatic, nuclear
A system: an object or group of objects; energy moves between stores when the system changes
Ways energy is transferred: by forces (mechanically), by an electric current, by heating, by radiation
Conservation of energy: energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred; the total stays the same in a closed system
ideas.taught: p1-energy-stores key point 3; p1-conservation key point 1 recalls it

ideas.name: Wasted energy is dissipated: spread out to the thermal store of the surroundings, hard to use
ideas.taught: p1-energy-stores key point 4; p1-conservation key points 2-3

ideas.name: Sankey diagram: arrow widths show input, useful and wasted energy
Ek = ½ m v²
Ep = m g h, g = 9.8 N/kg
A falling object: Ep lost = Ek gained (no air resistance)
Ee = ½ k e²; extension = stretched length − original length; limit of proportionality
Reducing unwanted transfers: lubrication (less friction), thermal insulation, streamlining
Thermal conductivity: higher means energy passes through the material faster; thicker walls of lower conductivity, slower cooling
efficiency = useful output energy ÷ total input energy (or useful power out ÷ total power in); never above 1 (100%)
Power: energy transferred each second, in watts (1 W = 1 J/s)
P = E ÷ t (and P = W ÷ t)
Work done: energy transferred by a force
Temperature (°C) shows how hot; a temperature change Δθ = final − start
ΔE = m c Δθ; specific heat capacity: energy to raise 1 kg by 1 °C (water 4200 J/kg °C)
Required practical: heater, joulemeter, thermometer, insulation; hazard; measured c too high because of losses
Internal energy and temperature: heating raises the particles' energy; temperature is linked to their kinetic energy
Energy resources: fossil fuels, nuclear, biofuel, wind, hydro-electricity, geothermal, tides, water waves, the Sun; renewable (replenished as it is used) vs non-renewable (finite)
Reliability (wind and solar are intermittent) and environmental effects (carbon dioxide and global warming, other pollution)
Current and potential difference, as much as the grid needs (full teaching is P2)
National Grid: power stations, step-up transformers, high-pd cables (smaller current, less energy wasted heating the cables), step-down transformers to homes
